CHIEF COMPLAINT
Yearly exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Beverly is a 24-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presenting for her yearly examination. She reports that she has been doing well overall. She began working in a bakery this summer, which she enjoys, but notes that proximity to desserts and treats has led to increased snacking and consumption of sweets during work shifts. She reports her blood sugars have been up and down, which she attributes to her diet. However, she confirms she has been taking her diabetes medication as prescribed without missing doses. She describes the temptation to eat desserts as challenging to resist. Her blood pressure has been good despite the fluctuations in blood sugar levels. She reports sleeping well with a full eight hours of sleep nightly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies any concerns about self-harm. No other additional concerns noted beyond those discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension
History of grade 2 systolic ejection fraction murmur (unchanged)

MEDICATIONS
Metformin twice daily
Lisinopril 10 mg once daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Currently employed at a bakery since summer, which she finds enjoyable. Sleeps eight hours nightly.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurological: Grips equal bilaterally. Able to feel light touch. Motor strength intact in lower extremities.
Cardiovascular: Heart regular rate and rhythm. Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur noted, unchanged from prior. No carotid bruits. Pulses good.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally.
General: No thyromegaly. No edema. Neurovascular exam intact.
Overall: Exam essentially normal.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1c: Elevated
Blood pressure: Normal/good
Vital signs: Within normal limits

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - Out of control. Goal hemoglobin A1c less than 7%, preferably under 6%. Plan: No medication changes at this time. Patient to reduce snacking and additional sweets. Patient to check fasting blood sugars in the morning and call in results in approximately two weeks. Follow-up visit in approximately two months to reassess. If hemoglobin A1c has not improved, will consider adding additional medication.

2. Hypertension - Stable and well-controlled. Plan: Continue current medication (lisinopril 10 mg once daily). No changes at this time.
